ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover the ultimate beneficial owner, all directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and franchise master licensee. Screening must run against the UN Security Council sanctions list, the US OFAC SDN list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Korea's own FSC-designated list. Additional checks include Interpol notices, Korea's Financial Action Task Force mutual evaluation follow-up lists, public corruption conviction databases, and adverse media on money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation financing, and fraud. Enhanced due diligence is required whenever a beneficial owner or director is a politically exposed person, a family member or close associate of a PEP, or a resident of a high-risk third country identified by the FATF. Hits must be documented with a reasoned disposition, escalated to the KOFIU and the firm's AML compliance committee, and resolved before any filing or capital contribution is made.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_qualifier: Beneficial ownership information is filed with the Korean registry and financial intelligence authorities and is not available through a general public search; notarized corporate certificates are disclosed to counterparties and banks only on a legitimate need-to-know basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Electronic Registration System / Korean Company Registry Name Search Portal (인터넷등기소)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Korean corporate name must be rendered in Hangul; a matching English transliteration may be registered as the trade name but the coexistence of a separate Hanja or foreign-language name is recognized as a secondary trade name. The name must contain the corporate form designator '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa) for a limited liability company. A proposed name may not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered company, trademark, well-known brand, or prohibited financial, medical, or public-purpose term, and must observe the four-tier ambiguity test: identical, confusingly similar, collaterally similar, and likely-to-deceive registrations. Foreign-language components must be transliterated to Hangul for registry approval and trademark clearance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain the written rejection reason from the registry, then submit a corrective name clearance application identifying two to five alternative names ranked by commercial viability. The applicant may also file a formal objection with the Supreme Court Registration Division or the relevant administrative authority within 30 days of rejection, attaching a supporting legal memorandum that distinguishes the proposed mark from prior registrations through phonetic, visual, conceptual, and trademark-database analyses. If rejection stems from a third-party trademark, the applicant may present a coexistence agreement or written consent from the rights holder, or amend the mark with a distinctive descriptive element and industry qualifier. The appeal must be submitted through the internet registry portal and followed by hard-copy filing with the court's registration officer, who must issue a written resolution within twenty business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are generally impermissible as the statutory registered address for a Korean fast-casual food franchise master licensing company. For the operating business scope of ISIC 5610, the National Tax Service and the local tax office require a physical premises that can accommodate the franchise headquarters functions, master licensee supervision, point-of-sale system administration, and compliance records. A virtual office postal address will be rejected during business registration (사업자등록) and license issuance because the registry demands proof of actual lease or ownership, facilities capable of storing books and records, and accessibility for tax inspections. A non-face-to-face corporation may be accepted only for limited holding or online-only entities, not for a food franchise master operation. A physical commercial lease must be in place before filing the corporate registry application, and the lease must be one of the mandatory attachments for business registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High likelihood of unannounced physical on-site inspections. Checklist: (a) verify the registered signboard corresponds to the corporate name; (b) inspect the business license displayed in a visible location; (c) confirm the presence of franchise management files, license agreements, royalty receipt system, and accounting records; (d) confirm adequate kitchen or commissary inspection documentation if any master training or food preparation occurs; (e) test POS and royalty wire payment interfaces; (f) check for a dedicated registered address rather than a shared mail panel. Quantified risk: the municipal tax office or Korean Immigration Service may inspect the premises within the first 180 days of registration, with a 30–45% probability for a food-service master entity; the National Tax Service may perform a local tax field inspection as part of the initial corporate tax registration review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended), especially the general provisions on companies (Articles 169 et seq.), provisions on Yuhan Hoesa limited liability companies (Articles 287 through 287-42), and the relevant registration procedure under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office address, e.g., Seoul Central District Court Corporate Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) together with the Application for Incorporation Registration filed with the District Court Corporate Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa; the total amount of contributions stipulated in the Articles of Incorporation must be actually paid (cash) or delivered (in-kind) before registration. There is no mandatory blocked escrow account, but the standard practice is to deposit the full cash contribution into a temporary corporate-formation account in the name of the representative member and obtain a bank certificate of deposit balance, which is later transferred to the corporate bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, THAT the incorporators and initial members of the Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), acting in a duly convened organizational meeting at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, after full deliberation, hereby adopt the following resolutions. FIRST, CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION AND SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: the initial capital of the company consists of the cash and in-kind contributions listed in the Articles; the representative member is directed to receive all contributions, to deposit cash into an escrow-like temporary account in the name of the promoter, to obtain an official bank deposit certificate evidencing full payment, and to prepare an in-kind contribution inventory report for any non-cash assets. SECOND, BANKING AUTHORIZATION: the representatives are jointly and severally authorized to open and maintain settlement and treasury accounts with any Korean licensed bank, to execute wire transfers and local remittances, to sign checks and promissory notes, to apply for corporate credit cards, and to manage the company's treasury; all disbursements exceeding the threshold set from time to time shall require joint signatures of the managing member and one other authorized representative. THIRD, REGISTERED OFFICE: the registered office set out in the Articles of Incorporation shall be adopted for all statutory and notification purposes; the representative is directed to register the address with the District Court Corporate Registry, the National Tax Service, and the local district office, and to secure certified evidence of lawful occupancy. FOURTH, STATUTORY AND CORPORATE OFFICERS: the initial managing member and any other officer appointed in the Articles or resolved by the members are each vested with all powers customary for their office; the managing member shall cause incorporation registration to be filed within the statutory period, and thereafter the company shall be bound by all lawful acts of such officers in the name of the company. FIFTH, OPERATIONAL AND LICENSING AUTHORIZATION: the managing member is authorized to execute the commercial lease, to enter into a master franchise licensing agreement for the self-serve broth bowl brand, to secure food service business report, fire safety certificate, environmental clearances, and occupational health approvals, and to open employer-registration files with the pension, national health insurance, and labor authorities. SIXTH, POST-INCORPORATION RATIFICATION: all pre-formation acts performed in the name or for the benefit of the company are ratified and adopted, and the officers are directed to pay all registration taxes, education surcharges, notary fees, franchise fees, and legal costs out of the company's funds. The meeting was then adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Foreign Investor Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of the registered office (e.g., Seoul Central Notary Public Office) and the designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Korean licensed legal preparer to draft the articles in Korean, including corporate name, registered office, purpose covering fast-casual self-serve broth bowl master licensing and restaurant operation, capital contribution schedule, method of calling members' meetings, director and managing member appointment method, and duration. The incorporators must certify their identities using a passport, foreigner ID, or Alien Registration Card, verify the right to use the registered office, and sign before a notary. If any member is a non-resident, file a foreign-investment report with the designated foreign exchange bank or the relevant financial regulatory electronic system before or within 30 days of incorporation. The notary then issues a constat and returns certified copies. This step is also the moment to conduct a brand-name conflict search at the Korean Intellectual Property Office on an optional but strongly recommended basis.
required_dossiers: Passport or Alien Registration Card of all incorporators
Copies of identification of in-kind property contributors
Power of attorney if any incorporator acts through an agent
Registered office lease agreement or certificate of real estate ownership
Foreign Investment Report form with proof of remittance if applying from abroad
Certificate of corporate seal impression and individual seals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the foreign exchange bank identifies a defect in the foreign-investment report or identity verification, correct the form and resubmit without penalty. If the registered office lease is inadequate, replace it with a formal irrevocable lease of at least one year and file the landlord's consent certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the Temporary Contribution Account and Depositing Cash and In-Kind Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial bank branch (for example, Shinhan, Kookmin, Hana, or Woori) and the Bank of Korea reporting system for currency transfer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation-preparation deposit account either in the name of the representative promoter or in the name of the future Yuhan Hoesa, as decided in the Articles of Incorporation. Transfer the cash contributions from each member through domestic remittance or an inbound foreign wire. The bank will issue a statement and a deposit confirmation showing the full amount held as at the date of registration. If the contribution includes in-kind assets such as kitchen equipment, leasehold interests, or a franchise license, the representative must complete an in-kind contribution audit report enumerating each asset, its valuation method, delivery date, and conformity with the Commercial Act valuation rules. After the corporate bank account is opened post-registration, transfer the temporary balance into the corporate account and obtain a closing statement.
required_dossiers: Pre-advice of inbound remittance or domestic transfer slips
Notarized Articles of Incorporation to establish account ownership
Passport or Alien Registration Card of the promoter
In-kind contribution inventory and independent appraisal certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a wire transfer is delayed or blocked by sanctions screening, provide source-of-funds documentation and a bank-specific SWIFT instruction code to clear the transfer. If the in-kind valuation is queried, obtain an independent appraiser certificate under the Commercial Act within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Incorporation Registration Application to the District Court Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registration Division of the District Court having the registered office address within its jurisdiction, for example, Seoul Central District Court Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization and completion of the capital contribution, file the Application for Incorporation Registration together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank deposit confirmation, the in-kind contribution audit report, the consent forms and acceptance oaths of the initial managing member and auditor, the proxy certificate if the filing is made by a legal preparer, and the receipt for the registration fee payment. The court scrutinizes the legality of the articles and the proof of contribution, enters the company into the corporate register, and issues a certified copy of the corporate registration certificate and corporate seal confirmation. The date of registration determines when the Yuhan Hoesa legally exists, after which the company may open its permanent bank account and begin licensed operations.
required_dossiers: Application for corporation registration on the court-prescribed form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank deposit confirmation and capital payment certificate
In-kind contribution report and appraisal documents, if any
Consent to appointment and oath of initial managing member and auditor
Power of attorney, if filing through a representative
Certified copy of the landlord's title and occupancy permission
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is suspended or queried, cure the deficiency within the court-designated period by filing supplementary documents such as a missing bank certificate or corrected articles. If the court rejects the application, file a motion for review and, if necessary, initiate a lawsuit against refusal of registration before the appellate court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Value-Added Tax Registration, and Tax Identification at the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office via the national HomeTax electronic system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after incorporation registration, submit a business registration application to the competent tax office, designating the representative member and place of business, choosing the tax type as value-added-tax taxable, and applying for an electronic tax invoice certificate. The application must be accompanied by proof of office ownership or lease, the corporate registration certificate, the corporate seal certificate, and the identification of the managing member. The tax office assigns a business registration number that must be displayed at the physical outlet. Register the business for local income tax and, if employees will be hired, register with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance programs. Open the permanent corporate bank account and file a new business value-added-tax schedule.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form
Corporate registration certificate
Corporate seal certificate and seal registration card
Lease agreement or ownership certificate for the restaurant premises
Bank account opening certificate
Passport or Alien Registration Card of the foreign investor
Parent establishment schedule if multiple outlets are planned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is deferred because of multiple business addresses, submit an amended lease and a floor-area statement. If the tax office queries the business category, reclassify under ISIC 5610 with a letter describing the self-serve broth bowl restaurant and master licensing model. A formal appeal may be submitted to the regional Tax Review Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Service Business Approval, Fire and Civil Defense Permit, Environmental Compliance, and Occupational Health Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local autonomous district office health and sanitation department, local fire station civil defense division, Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency, and Ministry of Environment-approved waste disposal authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the general restaurant business report under the Food Sanitation Act with the local district office before opening for trade, attaching the business registration certificate, floor plan, structural specifications, kitchen plan, menu list, and the food safety manager certificate if required. The district office may conduct an on-site facility and sanitation inspection. Submit building documentation to the fire station to obtain a fire safety certificate after inspection of extinguishers, exit routes, automatic kitchen suppression hoods, and high-pressure gas systems. File a waste producer report, a food waste recycling plan, and a wastewater discharge confirmation with the local sewerage authority. Secure a KOSHA occupational health verification for employees and a structural load inspection for the self-serve broth station.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate
Food service business report application form
Restaurant floor plan and kitchen drawings
Food safety education certificate for the responsible manager
Fire safety completion certificate and inspection records
Automatic extinguishing and kitchen hood system test records
Food waste disposal agreement with a licensed collector
Waste discharge report and sewerage confirmation
KOSHA occupational safety and health certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the district office orders facility supplementation, the operator has up to ten days to install the required equipment, after which a follow-up inspection is performed. If the fire safety certificate is withheld, replace or repair extinguishing equipment and re-submit the inspection request. If the environmental report is refused, renew the waste disposal contract and file a corrected report.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and the local autonomous district office food sanitation division; the Korea Fair Trade Commission for master franchise registration under the Fair Franchise Transactions Act
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Restaurant Business Report and Food Service Business License under the Food Sanitation Act; Master Franchise Registration Certificate under the Fair Franchise Transactions Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and the local sewerage and solid waste authorities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report not applicable; simplified environmental registration only. A street-level fast-casual restaurant is classified as a small-scale food-service facility. A project-level EIA is not required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, but the facility must submit food waste disposal and wastewater discharge reports and secure a sewerage discharge confirmation before opening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to the public sewer must meet the following effluent thresholds: biological oxygen demand no greater than 300 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand no greater than 400 mg/L, suspended solids no greater than 300 mg/L, total nitrogen no greater than 60 mg/L, total phosphorus no greater than 8 mg/L, pH 5.8 to 8.5, and fat oil and grease no greater than 90 mg/L. Food waste must be recycled or processed by a licensed contractor; residual waste must be transferred to licensed incineration. Cooking exhaust must pass through an oil mist filter with removal efficiency of at least 90 percent; volatile organic compound concentration in exhaust must not exceed 30 ppm.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and civil defense clearance includes a fire safety certificate from the local fire station under the Act on Fire Prevention and Installation, Maintenance and Safety Control of Fire-Fighting Systems; an automatic gas shut-off valve and cooking suppression system inspection; exit signage and evacuation lighting checks; a structural load inspection verifying that the broth station, mezzanine seating, and kitchen equipment floors can support the intended load; high-pressure gas and electrical safety inspections; and a Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency verification of workplace safety, food hygiene training, and designated food-safety manager certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, accessible through the HomeTax national electronic tax portal; export controls are reviewed with the Korea Customs Service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa LLC, complete Korean incorporation at the local court registry, obtain the corporate registration certificate, appoint a statutory representative (domestic tax representative for non-resident shareholders where required), then file the business registration application with the competent district tax office no later than 20 days from business commencement; the tax office assigns a 10-digit business registration number which serves as both the corporate Tax Identification Number and VAT registration number. Foreign investment must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if inward FDI report thresholds are met; notarized and apostilled/legalized charter, foreign shareholder identification, lease contract, and bank account evidence must accompany the application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Yuhan Hoesa LLC is a domestic Korean corporation taxed on worldwide income under the Corporate Income Tax Act, with no pass-through eligibility or special territorial exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or LLC pass-through election. Anti-hybrid mismatch provisions apply to deny deduction/non-inclusion outcomes where mismatched treatment arises.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) administered under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, with electronic tax invoices processed through HomeTax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for the corporate Yuhan Hoesa LLC; VAT registration is mandatory before business commencement. For individual sole proprietors, the simplified taxable person threshold is KRW 80,000,000 of annual taxable supplies, but registration is still required from business commencement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory national e-tax invoice regime: all taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices through the HomeTax e-tax invoice system and transmit them to the NTS within one business day after the supply date. No separate real-time fiscal stamping API exists; NTS clearance is achieved through mandatory digital invoice transmission, and franchise point-of-sale daily sales records must be reconcilable with electronic tax invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment is available for goods physically exported from South Korea under an accepted Korean customs export declaration, and for services supplied to foreign customers in foreign currency that are treated as exports under the Value-Added Tax Act (including qualifying overseas franchise licensing and royalty services, provided the service is performed/consumed outside Korea and the consideration is received in foreign currency).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Korean customs Export Declaration Form with assigned export declaration number)
Bill of Lading or equivalent sea/air waybill evidencing physical export
Foreign exchange bank inward remittance certificate (Korean Foreign Exchange Earning Confirmation or Foreign Currency Deposit Certificate) evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may disallow zero-rating upon audit if export documents are missing, false, or inconsistent. Unverified export zero-rating results in a retroactive VAT assessment at 10% plus interest and statutory penalty surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes; fraudulent export invoices or false foreign exchange certificates can trigger criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, restrictions on VAT refund claims, and disqualification from future zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Ministry of Economy and Finance, acting pursuant to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized yet carefully supervised foreign exchange regime. The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current-account transactions, including royalties, franchise fees, dividends, and trade-related settlements, subject to mandatory reporting through licensed foreign exchange banks. Capital-account transactions are generally free but require a declaration or ex-post reporting; certain inflows such as foreign direct investment, securities acquisition, and overseas borrowing require notification to the designated foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance. There is no broad surrender requirement for export proceeds, but foreign currency receipts must be repatriated into a domestic foreign currency account or a KRW account in a timely manner, typically within two years from the export declaration date, unless an extension is approved by the Foreign Exchange Bank. Profit remittances are permissible for non-resident shareholders under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, provided that the entity has submitted its capital registration, filed necessary tax returns (including withholding tax on dividends), and obtained a tax payment confirmation from the Korean National Tax Service. Dividend remittances are usually processed on the basis of a resolution of the shareholders meeting, audited financial statements, and a certificate of tax payment. The practical obstacle for a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa with a Chinese-linked ownership structure is not the legal convertibility of the KRW but rather the need to demonstrate the legitimate origin of the inbound capital, the authenticity of the licensing and royalty arrangements, and ongoing compliance with cross-border reporting obligations. Overall, the won is freely usable for trade and investment settlement within Korea, but strict paper trails are required for every remittance to avoid violation of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, anti-money laundering regulations, and U.S. secondary sanctions screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 14 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Enforcement Decree, exporters must receive export proceeds in foreign currency within the statutory collection period, generally no later than two years from the date of the export declaration, unless a shorter or longer period is established by the contract or approved by the Bank of Korea through a foreign exchange bank. Once collected, the proceeds must be physically deposited into a foreign currency deposit account maintained at a licensed Korean domestic banking institution or converted into Korean won at the prevailing market exchange rate. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; the exporter has the freedom to retain the foreign currency holding in the domestic account. However, the foreign exchange bank must be informed of the receipt, a foreign exchange sales confirmation must be obtained for the underlying transaction, and any extension beyond the deadline must be justified by exceptional causes such as force majeure or trade disputes. For the self-serve broth bowl licensing business, export proceeds would primarily arise from license fees, master franchise royalties, and the export of proprietary broth seasoning or machinery; all such foreign currency receivables must be collected and settled through a designated Korean foreign exchange bank and reported under the corresponding trade or service receipts codes.

Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: The viability of offshore fintech EMIs in South Korea is largely non-existent for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa seeking standard corporate banking services. A foreign EMI that is not licensed under the Korean Banking Act or the Electronic Financial Transactions Act cannot legally accept KRW deposits, maintain domestic bank account numbers, or provide corporate IBAN/KR-CDC clearing access in Korea. While global payment service providers such as Wise or Payoneer may offer ancillary cross-border settlement for outbound payments, they are not substitutes for a Korean won-denominated corporate bank account. Korean regulators mandate that all domestic businesses settle KRW obligations through a licensed bank, and any entity receiving foreign currency transfers must route those proceeds through a designated foreign exchange bank for Yuhan Hoesa. Furthermore, the Financial Services Commission and the Bank of Korea have repeatedly cautioned that unlicensed EMIs are barred from providing deposit-taking services to Korean residents. Even for travel-money or disbursement functions, the non-bank EMI would need to partner with a Korean bank, effectively preserving the bank as the account holder and subject to the same KYC and AML controls. Therefore, for this franchise licensing operation with regular inbound royalty wires, reliance on an offshore fintech EMI would be a regulatory red flag, likely triggering an automatic AML escalation and potentially invalidating the corporate entity's compliance posture. The optimal strategy is to use a Tier-1 Korean commercial bank as the primary operational and FX counterparty, with only limited and clearly designated utility payment or transit scenarios through a fully licensed money remitter if ever needed.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean financial institutions generally require the statutory representative director of a Yuhan Hoesa to appear physically in-branch during the initial corporate account opening, along with the company seal (corporate chop), certificate of seal registration, and original business registration certificate. For a wholly foreign-owned or non-resident-invested entity, the representative director must additionally provide a copy of their passport, proof of residency in Korea (a valid alien registration card or long-term visa), and a notarized or apostilled certificate of appointment if the directorship was resolved overseas. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for a standard fast-casual operating company under the current Financial Action Task Force-aligned Korean AML standards. A video interview may supplement, but not replace, the in-branch meeting. In exceptional cases where the representative director cannot travel, Korean law allows a power-of-attorney arrangement, but the attorney must be a Korean resident employee or director, and the bank will independently verify the identity, submit the original power of attorney with an apostille, and perform a direct telephone or video verification with the principal. The bank may also require the physical presence of the ultimate beneficial owner or the shareholder representative if the shareholding is concentrated. This mandatory in-branch appearance creates a non-waivable KYC defense layer and is intended to prevent the creation of shell or mailbox companies. For practical scheduling, the treasury team should plan for a minimum two-week branch appointment window at a major corporate branch of Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, or Hana Bank, with all corporate documents pre-translated into Korean or English under the bank's accepted language policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity: a non-resident Chinese shareholder or a multi-tiered corporate structure with nominees holding shares in a newly formed Korean Yuhan Hoesa constitutes a classic shell-entity red flag and is subject to the Korean Specialized Credit Financial Supervision Act and FATF Recommendation 24.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete notarized UBO declaration in Korean and English showing all natural persons with 10% or more voting rights; certified copy of the passport of each ultimate beneficial owner; the shareholder registry and memoriam of incorporation; a corporate organization chart up to the ultimate parent; bank and legal reference letters for the UBO with a source of wealth statement covering the last 24 months; apostilled power of attorney and directors' resolutions; and a sworn affidavit affirming no legal or professional relationship with politically exposed persons or sanctioned entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign capital injection from a Chinese jurisdiction through a wire transfer with an ambiguous purpose code, especially where the initial capital amount exceeds 100,000 USD without a prior foreign investment notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The original Foreign Investment Notification (foreigner status and capital subscription report) filed through the designated foreign exchange bank before the wire arrival; a capital subscription agreement signed by the non-resident investor; a SWIFT MT103 confirmation evidencing the remitting bank and the remitter's identity; the actual received foreign currency deposit voucher from the Korean bank; a Korean corporate bank statement showing the exact KRW exchange date and exchange rate; the minutes of the board meeting approving the issuance of shares; and a full capital verification report from a Korean certified public accountant if required by the bank's internal policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and transaction screening concern regarding Chinese-linked franchise and royalty payments, especially the movement of funds between Korean entity and China-based parent or master licensor, which may trigger enhanced due diligence on the nature of intellectual property transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of the master license agreement, franchise agreement, and trademark/patent registration certificates; a detailed fee schedule and royalty base calculation model with financial projections; signed non-assignment and non-sanctions representations from the licensor and investor; a list of all licensed counterparties and their jurisdiction of incorporation; evidence of any necessary technology transfer approval; and a written compliance opinion from a Korean attorney confirming the royalty stream is not a disguised capital flight or tariff evasion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive restaurant revenue profile mixed with foreign currency royalty inflows creates an inconsistency where the bank may suspect unreported operational income, cryptocurrency conversion, or conversion of unaccounted cash across borders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed cash management standard operating procedures, including daily point-of-sale reconciliation and cash-in-transit handling with a registered Korean security company; audited historical financial statements or a pro forma cash flow model demonstrating the expected POS cash ratio and royalty turnover; a list of all planned operational suppliers and their bank accounts; the entity's VAT filing receipts for the initial period after account opening; and a commitment letter to provide semi-annual accounting statements to the bank's compliance committee until the low-risk profile is established.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The economically compliant route for inbound capital injection into the Korean Yuhan Hoesa is through a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The non-resident shareholder or investor must first file a foreign investment notification with the transaction bank, specifying the nature of the investment, the amount, and the name of the Korean target company. Once the notification is accepted, the investor wires funds from an overseas bank account via SWIFT MT103 clearly referencing the purpose code 'investment in stock' and the assigned foreign investment notification number. The receiving Korean bank will credit the funds to a temporary foreign currency deposit account, then convert the USD or CNY to KRW at the market exchange rate and credit the entity's operating account only after all KYC and source-of-funds checks are cleared. For a cash contribution, the bank will also require the issuance of a capital contribution receipt and verification of the company's registered capital. For a non-cash contribution such as the licensing of the 'malatang' brand or self-serve flavor technology, the Korean authorities require a third-party valuation certificate and a report of the contribution through the Ministry of Economy and Finance. Any delayed notification may result in administrative fines and the refusal of the entity to benefit from foreign-invested-company preferences. Once the capital is verified, the company must register the foreign investment within 30 days? Actually the bank issues a certificate of registration, which is required for dividend remittance and later disposal of shares. For the inbound wire, the sender must ensure the remittance purpose is not worded as a loan or service fee, as that would change the legal classification and trigger a withholding tax and potentially a capital outflow restriction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and licensing disbursements must be routed through the commercial bank that holds the Yuhan Hoesa's operational account, subject to the bank's daily FX reporting to the Foreign Exchange Administration. For equipment procurement (such as broth dispensers, induction cookers, and ventilators) from suppliers in China or elsewhere, the preferred clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer for small shipments under USD 200,000, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) for larger or extended payment terms to protect against cargo risk, and a Documentary Collection for established repeat suppliers. Royalty and master licensing payments to a foreign parent or licensor should be executed via MT103 with the correct service code and a copy of the underlying license agreement, foreign exchange purchase voucher, and the bank's fully signed acknowledgment of the transaction. The Korean bank will require a tax payment confirmation for any overseas payment that triggers withholding tax, including royalty payments to non-residents, and will also check the beneficiary's name against international sanctions lists. For local outbound payments to domestic suppliers and staff, the standard rails are the Korean Electronic Banking System (Financial Information Network, K-FAST), which supports same-day KRW settlement. Cross-border disbursements for marketing and software licensing fees should be accompanied by the corresponding invoice and a Goods and Services description so the bank can assign the correct Foreign Exchange Transaction Report code. All outbound transfers exceeding the threshold (currently KRW 5,000 or USD 5,000 equivalent? More precisely, abroad payments over USD 5,000 must be reported at the time of remittance) are subject to real-time FX reporting through the bank's e-Tax and financial reporting system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts (with a Korean licensed bank) on a firm commitment basis against trade receivables, payables, and forecasted royalty inflows, with maturity not exceeding 12 months and requiring a confirmed underlying exposure.

FX swaps between KRW and the foreign currency using the corporate treasury account, permitted for both current and capital transactions but only when the counterparty demonstrates a genuine commercial need and the bank records the transaction under the appropriate hedging category.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) on any future external borrowings, subject to approval from the bank's market-risk committee and a clear linkage to funding for fixed asset investments or equipment leases.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not available as an onshore hedging instrument for a Korean resident with respect to KRW; use of offshore NDFs is legally barred for resident companies without special approval from the Bank of Korea, so they are not recommended in the treasury blueprint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Articles 60-61, Framework Act on National Taxes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - Korean Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the following fiscal year (calendar-year entity: March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 0.03% daily penalty on unpaid tax from day after due date to payment date (cap 365 days); 20% non-filing surcharge; 30% undisclosed income penalty; 40% understated income penalty; failure may trigger tax seizure and administrative cancellation of business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return (Local Income Tax Surtax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (provincial/city tax office) via NTS electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 following the fiscal year-end (calendar-year entity: April 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily late payment surcharge of 0.025% on unpaid local tax (cap 365 days); false or omitted filing attracts 20-40% penalties; continued non-payment causes property seizure and eventual strike-off of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return for the First Half (January 1 - June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service / applicable district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% of unpaid VAT assessed; daily late payment interest of 0.025% from due date; repeated delinquencies may lead to tax demand, suspension of business license, and administrative cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return for the Second Half (July 1 - December 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service / applicable district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% penalty on unpaid VAT; daily late payment interest of 0.025%; persistent non-compliance triggers tax seizure, revocation of the business license, and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Approval Resolution adopted at the Annual General Meeting of Members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders (members) of the Yuhan Hoesa; if mandatory audit applies, also file with the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) for public disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end (calendar-year entity: by June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For non-audited LLCs no direct court sanction, but failure to hold AGM may cause disqualification of directors; if audit is required and the audited statements are not submitted to FSS, administrative fines up to KRW 50 million; ongoing non-compliance may prompt the court to order correction or dissolve the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (Korean: 주식회사 등의 외부감사에 관한 법률), a Yuhan Hoesa LLC must appoint an independent CPA auditor if it meets any of the following criteria as of the end of the preceding fiscal year: (a) total assets exceed KRW 10 billion; (b) annual revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion; (c) average number of employees exceeds 100; or (d) total assets exceed KRW 5 billion and the company has related-party transactions of KRW 500 million or more. In addition, shareholders holding at least 10% of the equity may petition the court for a special audit under the Commercial Act if there is evidence of wrongdoing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for audited companies; non-audited small and medium-sized Yuhan Hoesa entities may apply the General Purpose Accounting Standards for SMEs (SME Korean GAAP). All financial statements must be prepared in accordance with the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and present a true and fair view.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a standalone public UBO register, but under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act, the company must verify and record beneficial owners whenever a member holds or acquires 10% or more of the equity, or exercises control. Any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be recorded in the corporate books and, where the transaction involves a Korean financial institution or triggers a report, reported to the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) within 30 days. Annually, the Yuhan Hoesa must attach a major-shareholder statement with its corporate income tax return, which serves as the de facto annual confirmation of beneficial ownership. Failure to maintain accurate UBO records or to report a reportable change may result in fines up to KRW 10 million and criminal liability for the responsible officer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 25,000 per audit (licensed Korean CPA firm)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national top marginal corporate income tax rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion; plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax amount, yielding an aggregate headline top rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive national rates: 9% for taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% for KRW 20 billion to KRW 30 billion; 24% above KRW 30 billion. Eligible small/medium enterprises may access reduced rates and temporary tax credits; free economic zone and foreign-invested high-technology projects can obtain 100%/50% corporate tax holidays for qualifying investment; R&D and job-creation tax credits are available under the Tax Incentive Limitation Law. No foodservice-specific patent box regime applies to a Malatang franchise, but franchise license fees paid to a qualifying foreign licensor may be taxable as royalties and subject to withholding and DTA treatment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (final CIT return Form 1) filed electronically through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final income tax return; corporations with fiscal years longer than six months must also file an interim semi-annual prepayment return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final CIT return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end taxpayer the deadline is March 31. The interim prepayment for the first six months must be filed and paid by August 31 for calendar-year corporations; for non-calendar fiscal years, the corresponding statutory due dates are the last day of the second month following the end of each six-month interim period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Tax Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Yuhan Hoesa, business registration number, head office address, representative director, tax year beginning and ending dates, and primary ISIC/NAICS codes (ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722513), plus shareholder ownership information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every non-resident shareholder and the country of tax residence. If a foreign parent or foreign ultimate beneficial owner holds 10% or more, attach the foreign ownership schedule and provide a written power of attorney naming the Korean tax agent. The filing director must certify that the beneficial ownership is accurate; a false certification exposes the signer to treaty-benefit denial and criminal tax-fraud liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Korean-source operating revenue: self-serve Malatang food sales recorded through POS, delivery orders, franchise royalties, branding and licensing fees, training fees, and any management or supply-chain fees received from related franchisees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all amounts in Korean won and reconcile daily POS Z-tapes and VAT schedules. If franchise royalties or license fees are paid from abroad to the Korean LLC, classify them under domestic-source income under the Corporate Tax Act and include a withholding reconciliation for any Korean tax paid by the remitter. Do not net out foreign taxes or intercompany offsets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of raw Malatang ingredients, meat, seafood, vegetables, dry noodles, soup-base sauces, spices, packaging, and direct labor consumed in food production and self-serve meal assembly.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases of soup-base concentrate, spices, or premade ingredients from a non-resident related supplier must be tested at arm's length using the CUP or TNMM method. The customs valuation for imported ingredients must match the transfer-priced invoice; inflated import prices are a common audit target and will be adjusted upward if the Korean LLC cannot prove independent comparability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Wages, rent, utilities, equipment depreciation, repairs, marketing, delivery platform commissions, professional fees, insurance, and deductible franchise management expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to a non-resident parent for headquarters management, centralized procurement, or IT services are deductible only if the services are actually performed, have economic substance, are not duplicated by local staff, and are priced under an arm's length fee schedule. Improper management-fee deductions are recharacterized as constructive dividends and are subject to additional withholding and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Non-Deductible Expenses, Tax-Exempt Income and Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible items such as entertainment and solicitation expenses over legal limits, tax penalties, undocumented cash payments, bribes, and over-accrued intercompany reserves; deduction of exempt income and special tax reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any undocumented purchases from related or unrelated suppliers are non-deductible and may trigger Value-Added Tax penalties. Interest paid to non-resident controlling shareholders is limited by thin capitalization: the debt-to-equity safe harbor is 3:1 (6:1 for banks/financial institutions), and interest exceeding that ratio must be included in this adjustment schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying NOL carryforwards, special deductions, exemptions, and all positive and negative adjustment schedules to the accounting net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 10-year loss carryforward is available only if the same business is continued and the ownership structure does not undergo a substantial change without business purpose. A Yuhan Hoesa that changes from Korean self-operated restaurants to a passive Malatang trademark shell may lose its NOL deduction. Attach the reconciliation of accounting income to taxable income with all cross-border adjustment items disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Computed Corporate Tax and Local Income Tax Surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive national CIT rates to the taxable income base; computation of the national corporate tax; computation of local income tax surcharge at 10% of national tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local income tax surcharge is computed on the actual national tax payable and must be reported to the local government on the same statutory deadline. A treaty reduction of the national withholding tax does not automatically reduce the local surcharge unless the treaty and domestic law provide a proportional local-tax reduction for the underlying payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for R&D expenditure, employment expansion, facility investment, foreign investment incentive credits in free economic zones, and any lawful tax-reduction or exemption items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean LLC owned by a non-resident is not automatically classified as a small/medium enterprise unless the consolidated group size satisfies Korean SME requirements. Claiming SME credits when the ultimate group exceeds the statutory size limits is fraudulent understatement and will be penalized. Maintain contemporaneous R&D and employment records if any credit is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Prepayments, Foreign Tax Credit and Net Tax Payable or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of interim prepayments, withholding taxes imposed on Korean-sourced income paid to the Korean LLC, foreign tax credits for qualified foreign-source income, and calculation of the final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Outbound dividend withholding taxes are not creditable on this corporate return; they are final taxes imposed on the non-resident shareholder and are to be reported through the separate withholding tax return. Do not double-count a foreign tax credit for taxes that are not economically borne by the Korean LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Related-Party International Transactions and Transfer Pricing Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of all cross-border related-party transactions: sales, purchases, royalty payments, interest, services, loan balances, and payments to related parties in tax havens; statement of TP adjustment amounts; checkbox for submission or readiness of Master File, Local File, and Country-by-Country report.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC must file the International Transaction Summary Statement even if no TP adjustment is made. If cross-border intercompany transactions exceed the statutory threshold (KRW 5 billion for Local File purposes), the Local File must be submitted within 30 days of notice; Master File and CbC reporting obligations follow group thresholds. A non-resident parent's failure to substantiate beneficial ownership or economic substance will cause treaty benefits to be denied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of the final CIT return attracts an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax; failure to file after receiving a notice or filing a fraudulent no-return is 40%; understatement of taxable income generally attracts 10% of the underpaid tax and 30% if fraudulently understated; late payment incurs a daily surcharge of 0.025% of the unpaid amount from the statutory due date to the payment date. Failure to prepare or submit transfer pricing documentation, or failure to file the required international transaction statement, can result in an additional 10% transfer pricing penalty on the related underreporting, in addition to ordinary understatement penalties. Deliberate tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act carries imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines of up to three times the evaded tax; aggravated cases involving amounts exceeding KRW 300 million can lead to imprisonment of up to 10 years under the Special Act on Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate on outbound dividends paid by the Korean LLC to a non-resident corporate shareholder, composed of 20% national Corporate Tax Act withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge, before any tax treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must be the beneficial owner of the dividend and have real economic substance in its residence jurisdiction. The mandatory procedure is: (i) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign
